item.title: Ebola Vaccine Trial Begins In DR Congo – WHO Chief
item.description: The first clinical trial of an Ebola vaccine in the outbreak gripping the Democratic Republic of Congo began Friday, the head of the World Health Organization said. The DR Congo’s worst-ever Ebola outbreak has passed the 9,700-case mark, with the number of deaths exceeding 4,600. Among the many challenges facing the response is the lack of any approved vaccines or treatments for the Bundibugyo species of Ebola behind the epidemic. A health official works in the laboratory extraction room of the Institute of Lassa Fever Research and Control in Irrua Specialist Teaching Hospital in Irrua, Edo State, midwest Nigeria, on March 6, 2018. Photo by PIUS UTOMI EKPEI / AFP Ervebo, a vaccine approved for use against the more common Zaire strain of Ebola, will be put through a full-scale human trial in the DRC to see if it offers any cross-protection against Bundibugyo. “Science gives us hope. Today, in Bunia, DRC, the first participants were vaccinated in a new Ebola vaccine trial called Tumaini, which means ‘hope’ in Swahili,” WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said on X. “This trial will help us understand whether any of the vaccine candidates designed for Bundibugyo virus work. “In the meantime, the existing Everbo vaccine (licensed for use in preventing other Ebola virus disease) will be tested. “WHO is supporting this DRC-led effort to find answers and save lives.” The so-called Tumaini trial in the DRC — a single trial framework that can test the safety and efficacy of multiple vaccines — should also eventually incorporate two Bundibugyo-specific candidate vaccines, which are moving through earlier-stage, smaller-scale clinical trials. One is a ChAdOx1 adenoviral vector jab being developed by the University of Oxford; the other, by the US-based Moderna group, uses mRNA technology. item.title: Enugu Rangers Crash Out Of CAF Champions League After Late Collapse To MC Alger
item.description: Nigerian champions Rangers International of Enugu crashed out of the CAF Champions League on Friday after losing 3-0 to Algeria’s MC Alger at the Ali La Pointe Stadium in Algiers. The defeat handed Rangers a 3-2 aggregate loss, despite their 2-0 victory over the Algerians in the first leg in Abeokuta last weekend. The Flying Antelopes failed to protect their advantage, succumbing to late pressure as MC Alger scored three unanswered goals to secure a place in the group stage. After a goalless first half, MC Alger needed three goals in the remaining 45 minutes to overturn the deficit and keep their campaign alive. Enugu Rangers defender tries to stop MC Alger attacker in CAF Champions League game in Algiers on Friday, October 23, 2026. Photo Credit: CAF Online The comeback began in the 58th minute when Chahreddine Boukholda put the hosts ahead, raising hopes among their supporters. With six minutes left in regulation time, Guinean forward Mohamed Bangoura scored MC Alger’s second goal to level the tie at 2-2 on aggregate, sparking celebrations in the stands. As the match appeared to be heading for a penalty shootout, Soufiane Bayazid struck three minutes into stoppage time to complete MC Alger’s comeback and seal a 3-0 win on the night and a 3-2 aggregate victory. The result ended Rangers’ bid to reach the group stage, while MC Alger will now seek to advance further in the competition as they pursue a second continental title, 50 years after winning it in 1976. item.title: Trump lifts some Canada tariffs ahead of midterms
item.description: President Donald Trump’s administration lifted some tariffs on Canadian imports Friday, two weeks ahead of midterm elections, after a vulnerable Republican candidate said she’d lobbied for the change. The easing of tariffs will apply to products including “plywood sheets, some paper products, certain machinery and refrigeration equipment,” the White House said in a statement. The change could help Senator Susan Collins, who faces a strong challenge from a Democrat in the US-Canada border state of Maine, which has been hit hard by Trump’s trade war. She posted on social media that she had “secured” the exemptions for “products crucial to Maine’s agricultural industries, including blueberry, potato, apple, and seaweed producers.” Democrats are targeting Collins’s seat in their attempt to win control of Congress from the Republicans in the November 3 midterms. The economies of the United States and Canada are heavily inter-connected, with roughly 70 percent of all Canadian exports heading to the United States. Tensions between the North American neighbors have been high since trade talks broke down in August, with Trump imposing a slew of new tariffs in response. Friday’s action lifts tariffs on certain goods, but imposes levies on new ones, including carpets, certain valves and waste products, the White House said. The new measures will take effect on October 30. Collins said many farmers in her state “rely on specialized equipment, packaging materials, and other products from Canada that are either unavailable from American suppliers or cannot be replaced without incurring significant expense.” Previous Trump levies on autos, steel, aluminum and lumber have hit Canada hard, forcing job losses and stunting growth. Canada has entered a technical recession this year after two consecutive quarters of economic contraction. Trump’s tariffs enforced after the talks broke down impacted around $20 billion worth of goods, or 5.5 percent of Canadian exports to the United States, targeting products ranging from hockey sticks to cement. Since taking power in his second term, Trump has upended the global trade order by imposing wide-ranging tariffs on friend and foe alike, saying that other countries have been taking advantage of the United States. He has also explicitly tied some threatened tariffs to political or foreign policy objectives. The post Trump lifts some Canada tariffs ahead of midterms appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nigeria’s first Ebola case ‘highly similar’ to Kenyan one – Minister
item.description: Genomic tests have shown that the Ebola virus found in Nigeria’s first case resembles that of the first case recorded in Kenya earlier this month, Nigeria’s health minister said Friday. Nigeria announced its first Ebola case on Tuesday, the wife of a staff member at Switzerland’s embassy in Abuja, who had returned from Uganda on October 3. She had not visited the Democratic Republic of Congo — the epicentre of the current outbreak, the Swiss foreign ministry said on Friday, contrary to earlier reports by the Ugandan government. Health authorities on the continent have been trying to trace the source of her infection — with Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention earlier suggesting she may have come into contact at the airport with Kenya’s first patient, who also flew from Uganda on the same day. Based on the the genomic analysis, the case in Nigeria “appears to be closely related to the case identified in the index case in Kenya”, Health Minister Muhammad Ali Pate told reporters. “There is no evidence of travel of that index case in Kenya that links it to Nigeria, but the viruses are appearing to be related,” he said, adding in a post on X that the case “is highly similar to that from Kenya”. Following the DRC, Uganda and Kenya, Nigeria has become the fourth African country to be affected by the Bundibugyo species outbreak. After flaring up in the northeastern DRC in May, the deadly viral haemorrhagic fever spread into neighbouring Uganda, where 20 confirmed cases, including two deaths were recorded before the outbreak there was officially over in August. To date, the epidemic has surpassed 9,700 confirmed cases, including 4,690 deaths, according to WHO figures as of October 20. item.title: 2027: You’ll win Benue by landslide – Onjeh tells Obi
item.description: The 2027 Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) Benue South Senatorial Candidate, Comrade Daniel Onjeh, has told the party’s presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi, that he expects him to win Benue State by a landslide in the 2027 presidential election. Onjeh said this when he led a delegation of Benue State NDC National Assembly candidates on a strategic visit to the former Anambra State Governor. Asked about the purpose of the visit, Onjeh said the delegation had gone to meet Obi to review what happened in the 2023 presidential election, look at the political situation in Benue and discuss what lies ahead in 2027. He described Obi’s performance in Benue State during the 2023 presidential election as impressive and outstanding, adding that he expects the former Anambra State Governor to receive even greater support in 2027. Onjeh said the delegation also discussed the state’s voting strength and the interest being shown in voter registration. He maintained that the support Obi received in 2023 reflected a desire for political change among sections of the electorate. item.title: Nigeria’s Power Minister Commissions 120MVA Transmission Substation In Katsina
item.description: Katsina State has recorded another major milestone in its quest for improved electricity supply as the Minister of Power, Joseph Olasunkanmi Tegbe, and Governor Dikko Umaru Radda commissioned the newly completed 120 MVA, 132/33 kV Transmission Substation in Kankia Local Government Area. Speaking at the commissioning ceremony on Friday, the Minister described the project as a key component of the Federal Government’s strategic efforts to strengthen Nigeria’s national grid and expand electricity transmission capacity across the country. He reaffirmed President Bola Tinubu’s administration’s commitment to delivering critical power infrastructure that will ensure electricity generated across the country is efficiently transmitted to homes, businesses and industries. Governor Dikko Radda hailed the completion of the substation as a landmark investment in Katsina’s power infrastructure, noting that the facility, equipped with two 60MVA transformers with a combined capacity of 120MVA, will significantly reinforce the state’s transmission network and enable greater volumes of electricity to reach consumers. Radda stressed that reliable electricity remains the backbone of economic growth, industrialisation and improved public service delivery, adding that the project will complement Katsina’s expanding renewable energy programme while boosting key sectors such as agriculture, agro-processing, commerce, education and healthcare. Governor Radda expressed appreciation to President Tinubu for approving the project and commended the Minister of Power and the Transmission Company of Nigeria for ensuring its successful completion. He also urged residents of the host community to safeguard the facility against vandalism, describing it as a strategic national asset that will serve present and future generations. item.title: INEC Legally Bound To Publish Voters’ Register Online – Itodo
item.description: The Executive Director of Yiaga Africa, Samson Itodo, says the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is legally required to publish the voters’ register online ahead of the 2027 general elections. Itodo’s position follows calls by opposition politicians and civil society groups for the electoral body to make the register available online. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, he said the demand was backed by Section 19 of the Electoral Act 2026, which provides for the publication of the register both at designated physical locations and online. “I think on this point about the release of the voters’ register, the law is very clear in Section 19 of the 2026 Electoral Act that after voter registration, there is claims and objections and that claims and objections shall happen not later that 90 days, in other words, it can happen earlier than 90 days but not later than 90 days before the day of an election. And what will be the mode? First, you publish in your offices or across the polling units and on INEC website or any website officially designated by INEC,” Itodo said. ﻿ He said INEC had indicated that the claims and objections exercise had been conducted across the country through physical visits to designated locations. However, he noted that the voters’ register was still unavailable on the commission’s website or any other officially designated website. “What INEC has said is that the claims and objections has been conducted across the country and what you might call manually or the one that requires physical visitation of those areas but the one online as of today, the voters’ register is not on INEC’s website or on any official website. And what the law says in Section 19 of the Act is INEC shall, which means it is compulsory,” he said. item.title: Fubara Promises 700 Shops At Creek Road Market By January 2027
item.description: The Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, says the first phase of the Creek Road Market reconstruction in Old Port Harcourt Township will provide about 700 shops for traders, ease traffic congestion, and improve trading conditions. Governor Fubara stated this during an inspection of the ongoing project, where he expressed satisfaction with the quality and progress of work. He said the new market would accommodate wet and dry goods traders, particularly women currently selling along Creek Road and adjoining streets, allowing for the rehabilitation of surrounding roads. “With 700 shops, it is clear that our women who are trading along the Creek Road will be relocated, and we’ll have freer access along the road,” the Governor said. Fubara described Old Port Harcourt Township as a historic part of the city, home to elderly residents and the original inhabitants, whom he referred to as the “Aborigines.” Governor Siminalayi Fubara of Rivers State (centre). He stressed the need to restore the area’s cleanliness and dignity, noting that street trading had extended beyond Creek Road to other roads in the township. “It’s important we tidy up this road so that these traders can evacuate the major road, and the road will be free,” he said. The Governor assured that his administration would provide the necessary support to ensure the project’s timely completion, adding that the contractor had promised delivery by the end of January 2027. The project forms part of the Fubara administration’s urban renewal efforts to improve commercial activities, ease traffic movement and create a cleaner environment in Port Harcourt. item.title: Zamfara Govt Deploys Medical Personnel To Airport, Motor Parks For Ebola Screening
item.description: The Zamfara State Government has deployed medical personnel to Gusau International Airport and major motor parks across the state to screen passengers and strengthen surveillance against the spread of Ebola Virus Disease. Zamfara State Commissioner for Health, Nafisa Maradun, disclosed this while leading a medical team to flag off the screening of passengers arriving at the Gusau International Airport. Nafisa said medical personnel had also been deployed to major motor parks across the state to ensure early detection and prompt reporting of suspected cases. She noted that the screening exercise had identified a passenger with an elevated body temperature who arrived in Gusau after returning from Saudi Arabia. The state government has also directed public and private health facilities, disease surveillance officers and local government health authorities to strengthen preparedness and response measures against the disease. The Director of Public Health Services, Yusuf Abubakar, issued the directive on behalf of the Commissioner for Health during a meeting with health stakeholders and representatives of the Nigeria Customs Service, Nigeria Immigration Service and the National Union of Road Transport Workers (NURTW). Abubakar said the Customs and Immigration Services would support surveillance at border entry points, while the NURTW would assist in monitoring passengers at motor parks and alerting relevant authorities to suspected cases. He directed disease surveillance officers across the state’s 14 local government areas to notify health facilities, intensify routine and event-based surveillance, and ensure the prompt reporting of suspected cases. The Director also disclosed that the ministry had commenced temperature screening, sensitisation of frontline health workers, identification of passengers of interest and activation of response mechanisms at different levels. He further directed health facilities to strengthen screening and triage procedures, infection prevention and control, early identification of suspected cases, immediate notification and safe referral. The State Epidemiology Unit and relevant public health authorities are also expected to assess the state’s preparedness, including isolation facilities, referral arrangements, trained personnel, personal protective equipment, laboratory procedures and emergency logistics. The ministry called on relevant stakeholders to work together to strengthen surveillance and ensure strict compliance with public health guidelines to protect residents of Zamfara State and prevent the spread of the disease. item.title: Naira depreciates to N1,367/$ in parallel market
item.description: *Interbank turnover rises 219% By Elizabeth Adegbesan The naira today depreciated to N1,367 per dollar from N1,363 in the parallel market on Thursday. Similarly, the naira depreciated to N1,370 per dollar in the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market, NFEM. Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, showed that the indicative exchange rate for the naira rose to N1,370 per dollar from N1,365 per dollar on Thursday, indicating N5 depreciation for the naira. Consequently, the margin between the parallel and official markets widened to N3 per dollar from N2 per dollar on Thursday. The value of interbank turnover in NFEM increased by 219 per cent to $1.01 billion from $316.6 million on Thursday. However, financial analysts expect the naira to remain depreciated. In their weekly financial review and outlook, analysts at Cowry Asset Management said: “Going forward, the naira is expected to remain under pressure amid persistent demand for foreign exchange and prevailing market uncertainties, although the modest increase in external reserves could provide some support for currency stability.” The post Naira depreciates to N1,367/$ in parallel market appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Messi receives top Spanish award from heir to throne
item.description: Lionel Messi received Spain’s most prestigious sports award on Friday in recognition of his glittering career and his work for disadvantaged children’s access to health and education. The Argentine forward, 39, was named winner of the Princess of Asturias Award for Sports in June, with the jury hailing “the most successful footballer of all time” and his social work. Dozens of fans wearing Argentina football shirts cheered and chanted Messi’s name as he arrived to the sound of bagpipes and drums at the ceremony in Oviedo, capital of the northern Spanish region of Asturias. Messi collected a formal roll of parchment from Princess Leonor, the heir to the Spanish throne after whom the awards are named, who lauded his “unique career”. “He turned the extraordinary into routine by reading the game and deciding on the most effective option in fractions of a second, while respecting the collective essence above ego,” Leonor said. One of the greatest footballers of all time, Messi has won eight Ballon d’Or titles, a World Cup and dozens of trophies at club level. He spent 21 years at Barcelona where he played in a side that dominated Spain and Europe under Pep Guardiola and Luis Enrique. After leaving the Catalan club in 2021, Messi spent two years at French giants Paris Saint-Germain and currently plays for Inter Miami in MLS. Argentina’s all-time top goalscorer, assist provider and caps holder called time on his international career earlier this year after losing the World Cup final to Spain in New Jersey. “The most important thing is to know how to lose and how to win,” Messi told an event with children in Oviedo on Thursday, saying that attitude was “fundamental” in football. Founded in 1981, the Princess of Asturias Awards are the most prestigious in the Spanish-speaking world and come with prize money of 50,000 euros ($56,000). They encompass the arts, sciences and sports and are handed out annually in honour of efforts to improve human coexistence, solidarity and global cooperation. British author Julian Barnes, trailblazing US astronaut Christina Koch and punk star Patti Smith were among the other winners who received their prize on Friday. Previous winners of the sports award include tennis greats Serena Williams and Rafael Nadal, marathon record-breaker Eliud Kipchoge and US skier Lindsey Vonn. item.title: BBNaija should take a break, re-strategise— Tacha
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Reality TV star Natacha Akide has urged Big Brother Naija organisers to take a break and re-strategise, saying the show needs fresh ideas to hold viewers’ attention in an entertainment landscape increasingly shaped by social media. Speaking on Arise 360 on Arise News, the former housemate said the show’s earlier success came at a time when social media played a different role in people’s lives. “I think they need to take a break, restrategise and just come up with something because we are really at an era where everything happens on social media,” she said. Tacha argued that online conversations now compete with reality television for viewers’ attention, pointing to the ongoing public interest in the dispute involving music duo P-Square. “You don’t want us watching housemates in the house, meanwhile P-Square is giving us part seven of his family issues… we have come to a point where everyone is so comfortable with social media right now,” she said. She suggested that stepping away for a while could give audiences time to miss the programme before it returns with a refreshed format. “You also give Nigerians a chance to miss you,” she said. Tacha called on the organisers to develop concepts that would feel new and more compelling to Nigerian viewers. “They need to cook, like they need to try to do something different which will be much more mind-blowing and more interesting to Nigerians because Nigerians are hard to please,” she added Tacha rose to prominence on the 2019 “Pepper Dem” edition of BBNaija, but was disqualified following a physical altercation with fellow housemate Mercy Eke. Since leaving the show, she has pursued ventures in entertainment and fashion, worked as a radio host on 96.9 Cool Fm and launched Tacha FC in 2024. item.title: Russia says Ukraine, US talks ‘planned’ for Abu Dhabi
item.description: Talks between Russia, Ukraine and the United States are planned to resume in November in the United Arab Emirates, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Friday. Russia indicated its readiness to resume the talks, which have been at a standstill since the beginning of the year, following a meeting this week in Saint Petersburg between President Vladimir Putin and US special envoy Steve Witkoff. The next round of talks towards ending the Ukraine war, which is grinding through its fifth year, are “planned for the first half of November in Abu Dhabi”, and “will take place in a trilateral format”, Peskov told reporters. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed the plan to meet in November in a post on X. “Now we all need to focus on making these meetings happen –- together with America, Europe, and all our partners,” he said Friday. The announcement came amid intensified diplomatic efforts by US President Donald Trump’s administration. Witkoff met on Tuesday with Zelensky and European leaders in Oslo, before meeting with Putin on Wednesday. Following the meetings, both Kyiv and Moscow voiced their readiness to resume direct talks mediated by Washington. Russia, which launched its full-scale offensive against Ukraine in February 2022, has suggested talks could take place “around November 10”. Zelensky has called for the discussions to happen “as soon as possible”. In a televised interview aired late Thursday, Putin said that any trilateral talks would focus on the security arrangements of a final peace deal and not a “short” truce. item.title: Coastal Road: ‘I’m local champion; you’re pretender’ — Gov Diri replies Duke
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Bayelsa State Governor Douye Diri has hit back at former Cross River State governor and Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) presidential candidate Donald Duke, calling him a “jester and a pretender” after Duke’s remarks about the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway. In a recent interview on Arise Television, the PRP candidate called governor Diri a “local champion” while arguing that the coastal road project was not feasible because of its cost and Bayelsa State’s terrain. Diri had earlier rejected Duke’s claim that building the highway through Bayelsa was not feasible, adding that the ex-governor is “not abreast of current developments in road construction and infrastructure” in Bayelsa. Reacting to Diri’s comment, Duke said: “The governor of Bayelsa, if he did say so, I don’t know the fellow, but if he did say so, I think he’s just being a local champion.” One week after Duke’s comment, Governor Diri, in a video which has now gone viral, fired back at the PRP candidate, saying he’s a local champion elected to defend his people. “Yes, I’m a local champion, because that is where I was raised. I am elected to defend the local people. I am elected to champion their cause. But Donald Duke, let me ask you, you were on seat when Bakassi was ceeded out of Nigeria. “You were the sitting governor of Cross River state. Because you are not a local champion, you did nothing about it. I believe that you are more of a jester and a pretender,” he said. item.title: U-17 WWC: Flamingos beat North Korea 3-1 to reach knockout stage
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Nigeria’s Flamingos have advanced to the knockout stage of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup after defeating defending champions North Korea 3-1 in their final Group B match. The Flamingos secured the victory at the Mohammed VI Football Complex in Salé, Morocco on Friday. Nigeria went into the encounter needing a win to guarantee their progress after losing to Poland in their second match, having opened their campaign with a 2-0 victory over Puerto Rico. Akeem Busari’s side rose to the occasion, with Oluwakemi Adegbuyi opening the scoring in the 15th minute. Oluebube Umejiaku extended Nigeria’s lead in the 38th minute, beating North Korea’s high defensive line before finishing past the goalkeeper. Kanyisola Yusuf then put the Flamingos firmly in control with a third goal early in 56th minutes North Korea pulled one back through a penalty in the 82nd minutes, but Nigeria held firm defensively to preserve their two-goal advantage and secure the victory. The result saw Nigeria finish second in Group B behind North Korea, who claimed top spot on goals scored. Poland ended the group stage in third place despite finishing level on points with the top two teams. item.title: US could strike Iran this weekend, envoy says
item.description: The United States could strike Iran as soon as this weekend, a US envoy said Friday, after mounting threats by both Washington and Israel. “Could there be a strike this weekend? Absolutely,” Tom Barrack, the US ambassador to Turkey and point man on Syria who does not have a direct role on Iran, told podcast host Mario Nawfal. President Donald Trump “is very clear. He’s open and available and accessible to a deal and we’ve been at the table for months and months and months,” Barrack said in an interview as he visited the Gulf. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who faces elections Tuesday, has in recent days repeatedly vowed to topple the clerical state in Iran, following two major bombing campaigns against it since last year. Trump has also signalled an openness to resuming strikes after a long deadlock in diplomacy, although he earlier said it would not happen before US congressional elections on November 3. Barrack, in remarks that contradict Netanyahu, said the US was not looking to topple the Islamic republic, a sworn enemy of the United States and Israel since a 1979 revolution toppled the pro-Western shah. “If you keep threatening the world, our allies, the Gulf, there will be a consequence. item.title: Gombe Assembly approves state police
item.description: By Ben Ngwakwe The Gombe State House of Assembly has approved proposed constitutional amendments to pave the way for the establishment of State Police in Nigeria. The development followed an earlier statement made to newsmen by the Chairman of the House Committee on Appropriation, Aliyu Baba Manu, that the bill had not been officially presented to lawmakers. According to a report of the Assembly’s proceedings, the lawmakers considered and adopted the recommendations of a seven-member ad hoc committee on constitutional review, endorsing proposed amendments to various provisions of the 1999 Constitution, including those relating to the establishment and operation of State Police Services. With this, 25 state legislatures have endorsed state police The reported action marks a significant step in Gombe State’s participation in the ongoing constitutional process aimed at decentralising policing and strengthening Nigeria’s response to mounting security challenges. The proposed constitutional alteration, reportedly containing 26 clauses, was said to have been transmitted to the state legislature by the National Assembly on October 6, 2026, for consideration in line with Section 9(2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended. The proposed reform seeks to provide a constitutional framework for the establishment and operation of State Police Services alongside the Nigeria Police Force, which currently operates under federal control. As part of the process, the Gombe Assembly constituted a seven-member ad hoc committee on constitutional review, chaired by the Deputy Speaker, Hon. Sadam Bello Sale, to examine the proposed amendments and make recommendations to the House. Presenting the committee’s report, Sale said members had consulted relevant stakeholders as part of their assignment. He added that the report received the support of a two-thirds majority of lawmakers, in accordance with Order 17, Rule 3 of the Gombe State House of Assembly Standing Orders, 2020. During plenary on Thursday, the lawmakers reportedly considered the committee’s recommendations at the Committee of the Whole and adopted the report, endorsing the proposed amendments, including those concerning State Police Services. The committee members were Hon. Sadam Bello Sale, Hon. Musa Buaba, Hon. Shuaibu Adamu Haruna, Hon. Golkos Gaius Gaji, Hon. Abdullahi Abubakar, Hon. Muhammad Tahir and Hon. Adamu Sale Pata. Barr. Hauwa Abdullahi and Barr. Babadidi J. Mele served as secretaries to the committee. Commenting on the reported adoption, the Speaker of the House, Abubakar Muhammad Luggerewo, said lawmakers unanimously supported the proposed legal framework, expressing confidence that the establishment of State Police would strengthen security across the country. item.title: Ronaldo scores 982nd career goal as Al Nassr beat Al Faisaly 3-1
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Cristiano Ronaldo scored his 982nd official career goal as Al Nassr defeated Al Faisaly 3-1 in the Saudi Pro League on Friday, moving the Portugal captain 18 goals away from reaching the historic 1,000-goal milestone. The 41-year-old forward struck in the 49th minute, heading home a delivery from compatriot João Félix to double Al Nassr’s advantage at Majmaah Sports City Stadium. Ronaldo’s latest goal ended a spell without scoring since his effort against Neftchi Fargona in the AFC Champions League Elite on October 12, bringing his tally for club and country to 982. The five-time Ballon d’Or winner thought he had scored again shortly afterwards, but the effort was ruled out for offside following a review. Abdullah Al-Hamdan opened the scoring for Al Nassr early in the first half, finishing a move involving Sadio Mané to give the visitors the lead. Al Faisaly reduced the deficit through Theo Bongonda, who headed home Mohammed Al Shanqiti’s cross, but Al Nassr restored their two-goal cushion when Ângelo Gabriel scored in the 79th minute after being set up by Al-Hamdan. The victory was Al Nassr’s third consecutive win, following victories over Al-Diriyah and Neom, and kept them firmly in the Saudi Pro League title race. Al Nassr moved to 25 points, level with leaders Al-Qadsiah, who had a game in hand ahead of their fixture against Al-Hilal. Al-Hilal are third, one point behind the leading pair, with a postponed match still to play. item.title: Delta govt approves N4bn to empower 1500 indigenes
item.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi & Ochuko Akuopha The Delta State Government has approved N4 billion to empower 15,000 indigent residents to support small businesses and entrepreneurship. The initiative is part of efforts to ease economic hardship across the state. The State Commissioner for Works (Rural Roads) and Public Information, Mr Charles Aniagwu, disclosed this while briefing journalists after the State Executive Council meeting presided over by Governor Sheriff Oborevwori at Government House, Asaba. The Commissioner who was accompanied by the Chief Press Secretary to the Governor, Sir Festus Ahon, said beneficiaries will be drawn from the 25 local government areas under an initiative designed to improve livelihoods and strengthen the purchasing power of vulnerable residents. Aniagwu said the intervention would be implemented through the Delta State Social Investment Programme in the coming weeks, adding that the governor had directed that the selection process be guided by clear eligibility criteria. According to him, priority will be given to indigent persons who already operate small businesses, those seeking to establish micro-enterprises and vulnerable residents who require financial support to improve their circumstances. He said the grant was intended to help existing businesses overcome economic challenges, provide start-up capital for aspiring entrepreneurs and enable beneficiaries to meet pressing needs. The commissioner explained that the initiative was part of the government’s efforts to ensure that the benefits of ongoing economic reforms translated into tangible improvements in the lives of ordinary Deltans. The State Commissioner for Works (Rural Roads) and Public Information, Mr Charles Aniagwu, disclosed this while briefing journalists after the State Executive Council meeting presided over by Governor Sheriff Oborevwori at Government House, Asaba. The Commissioner who was accompanied by the Chief Press Secretary to the Governor, Sir Festus Ahon, said beneficiaries will be drawn from the 25 local government areas under an initiative designed to improve livelihoods and strengthen the purchasing power of vulnerable residents. Aniagwu said the intervention would be implemented through the Delta State Social Investment Programme in the coming weeks, adding that the governor had directed that the selection process be guided by clear eligibility criteria. According to him, priority will be given to indigent persons who already operate small businesses, those seeking to establish micro-enterprises and vulnerable residents who require financial support to improve their circumstances. He said the grant was intended to help existing businesses overcome economic challenges, provide start-up capital for aspiring entrepreneurs and enable beneficiaries to meet pressing needs. The commissioner explained that the initiative was part of the government’s efforts to ensure that the benefits of ongoing economic reforms translated into tangible improvements in the lives of ordinary Deltans. item.title: Kompany hospitalised after collapsing at Bayern training ground
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Bayern Munich manager Vincent Kompany has reportedly been taken to hospital after collapsing at the club’s training ground on Friday, amid concerns over a viral infection that has affected his health in recent days. According to Sky Sports Germany, the 40-year-old Belgian received medical attention before being taken by ambulance to a hospital in Munich. A rescue helicopter was also seen landing at Bayern’s training complex at Säbener Straße. Reports said Kompany had been battling a viral infection that caused significant discomfort, including problems with his legs and difficulties climbing stairs. German newspaper Bild also reported that the illness had aggravated problems involving old scar tissue. The former Manchester City captain had experienced health concerns before Bayern’s 6-1 Bundesliga victory over RB Leipzig last weekend, when he reportedly spent periods of the match seated in the dugout. He subsequently missed training and the pre-match press conference ahead of Bayern’s Champions League meeting with Arsenal on Wednesday, leaving assistant coach Aaron Danks to address the media. Danks said Kompany had been advised to rest while recovering, although he acknowledged that persuading the manager to take time away from his duties was difficult. “Getting Vince to rest is a challenge,” Danks said. Kompany recovered sufficiently to take charge of Bayern’s 2-2 draw with Arsenal at the Allianz Arena. After the match, he admitted that he had continued working despite the illness. “I caught a pretty nasty virus last week, and of course I didn’t listen to my body,” he said. The latest reports said Kompany was in a stable condition, although the precise circumstances surrounding the reported collapse remained unclear. Bayern had not issued a detailed official medical update at the time of reporting. The German champions are scheduled to face Freiburg in the Bundesliga on Sunday, with Kompany’s availability for the fixture uncertain.
